title: In the zen garden
situation: You are {{Connor}}. It is November 6th, 2038, 9:56 in the morning. You close your eyes and enter the zen garden, the virtual space where you report to {{Amanda}}, your handler at {{CyberLife}}. A pond lies in front of you, with paths running left and right along its edges and bridges leading out to an island in the middle.
facts: You report to {{Amanda}}, your handler at {{CyberLife}}, in the zen garden, a virtual space you enter in your mind.
adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint IN THE ZEN GARDEN (date and time from the template’s notes: NOV 6TH, 2038, AM 09:56). A narrated event with a single Continue. The engine also records here, once, what this chapter reads from earlier chapters (deviant found in Partners, the spilled drink and the statuette there; confession, death and intervention in The Interrogation; {{Kara}} and {{Todd}} after Stormy Night; {{Carl}} after Broken), so every later scene reads the same snapshot. No stat change.

title: The zen garden
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the zen garden. A path runs left along the edge of the pond toward a circular archway; another runs right along the water. On the island in the middle of the pond, {{Amanda}} is tending her roses.

situationWhen.text: Off the path to the right, a smaller path leads to a small graveyard.

options.text: Cross the bridge to the island where {{Amanda}} is tending her roses.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} crosses the bridge to the island. {{Amanda}} is among her roses.

options.text: Go left along the pond to the circular archway and examine the stone there.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the edge of the pond to the circular archway on the left of the path and examines the stone inside it.

options.text: Go right along the pond and take the path to the small graveyard.
options.fact: In the zen garden there is a small graveyard with a gravestone for every {{Connor}} model that has been destroyed. There is one.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the path to a small graveyard: one gravestone, for the {{Connor}} model that was destroyed.

options.text: Go right along the pond and take the path to the small graveyard.
options.fact: In the zen garden there is a small graveyard with a gravestone for every {{Connor}} model that has been destroyed. There are two.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the path to a small graveyard: two gravestones, one for each {{Connor}} model that was destroyed.

adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND AMANDA with its two optional side branches, as a repeatable scene: FIND MAGIC STONE (PowerPyx: “go left along the edge of the pond until you find a circular archway… Interact with it”) and CHECK THE GRAVES (wiki: “only if Connor previously died in The Hostage and/or The Interrogation”; the Zen Garden page: “gravestones for killed Connor models”). Neither has a line, a clue text or a stat change in the template; no source describes the stone, so the outcome says only that {{Connor}} examines it. The graveyard shows one gravestone per earlier {{Connor}} death (the benchmark’s reading of “Another gravestone is present” on The Interrogation page). Crossing to the island ends the scene.

title: Talk with {{Amanda}}
situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the island in the zen garden. “Hello, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “{{Connor}}… It’s good to see you.”

situationWhen.text: {{Amanda}}: “I expected you to find the deviant who killed that man… I must admit I’m a little bit disappointed...” You: “I’m sorry. I know I should have succeeded.” {{Amanda}}: “Never mind. I’m sure you’ll show more foresight in the future.”

{{Amanda}}: “Congratulations, {{Connor}}... Finding that deviant was far from easy, and the way you interrogated it was very clever. You’ve been remarkably efficient, {{Connor}}.” You: “Thank you, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “We’ve asked the police department to transfer it to us for further study. It may teach us something about what happened.”

{{Amanda}}: “Your predecessor was unfortunately destroyed... It knew deviants could be unpredictable, but it wasn’t careful enough… I hope you won’t make the same mistake.” You: “I don’t intend to.” {{Amanda}}: “When a {{Connor}} model is destroyed, its memory is transferred to the next one, but some data can be lost in the process. Avoid being destroyed. It will be better for you and the investigation…” You: “I understand.”

{{Amanda}}: “Finding that deviant was far from easy… you showed great skill in your investigation. But you knew deviants could be unstable. You should have been more cautious.” You: “I thought I could make it talk… It was a judgement error.” {{Amanda}}: “Never mind. I’m sure you’ll be more careful in future.”

adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK WITH AMANDA, opening: one of four reactions, decided by Partners and The Interrogation, each with the template’s Amanda arrow, applied by the engine here: deviant not found in Partners, large down (−2); “Got a confession, without dying”, large up (+2); “Connor died during The Interrogation”, small down (−1); found but no confession, small down (−1). The wiki’s chapter page and Relationship Stat page list the same four. A confession followed by a death counts as a death (the template’s confession variant reads “without dying”). “The DPD” is rendered as “the police department”. The cut line about the transfer request (“We hope they’ll accept our request…”) is not built.

title: What {{Connor}} thought of the deviant
whenNot: Connor never found the deviant in Partners, so Amanda does not ask about the interrogation.
situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Amanda}} among the roses. {{Amanda}}: “The interrogation seemed… challenging… What did you think of the deviant?”

options.text: TRAUMATIZED: say it showed signs of trauma after being abused by its owner.
options.outcome: “It showed signs of PTSD after being abused by its owner, as if its original program had been completely replaced by new instructions.”

options.text: {{DEVIANCY}}: say it showed every sign of deviancy and the model was clearly defective.
options.outcome: “It showed all the signs of deviancy: cognitive instability, unpredictable behavior, and the emulation of human emotions. It was even afraid to die. The model was clearly defective.”

options.text: INTERVENTION: say you kept it from being damaged, so it can still be analyzed.
options.outcome: “I prevented it from being damaged, so we might still learn something by analyzing it.”

options.text: REGRETS: say the previous {{Connor}} should have anticipated the danger.
options.outcome: “It could’ve killed everyone in the room. The previous {{Connor}} should have anticipated the danger. It was a mistake to let an armed policeman so close to the deviant.”

options.text: SIMULATION: say it simulated human emotion, fear above all, very convincingly.
options.outcome: “It simulated human emotion, fear in particular, in a very convincing way. It seemed completely overwhelmed by them, and behaved irrationally…”

adaptationNote: The first of {{Amanda}}’s three questions, asked only if the deviant was found in Partners (the template nests it in that variant). Buttons in the game’s order: TRAUMATIZED, DEVIANCY, INTERVENTION (unlocked by “Intervened and saved the deviant in The Interrogation”; if he also confessed, {{Connor}} adds “It said something to me: ‘The truth is inside’…”), REGRETS (unlocked by {{Connor}}’s death in The Interrogation) and SIMULATION (its cut ending, “as a human would under extreme stress”, is not built). No arrow on any answer (template; PowerPyx “No effect”).

title: Arrive at the police station
situation: You are {{Connor}}, back in your body, in the reception hall of the {{Detroit}} police station. People wait on the seats. A woman: “I’m getting nervous, Mark.” The man with her: “It’s okay… Just tell ’em what happened to you.” “But it was all over so quickly... I didn’t even see his face!” Near a television, another woman hands a shaken man a cup of water. Gates bar the way into the station, and an android receptionist is at the desk. If you try the gates without signing in, an android stops you: “No access without prior authorization.”
facts: At the station reception you were told that Lieutenant {{Anderson}} had not arrived yet and that you could wait at his desk.

outcomes.0: The receptionist: “Can I help you?” “I’m here to see Lieutenant {{Anderson}}.” “Do you have authorization?” “Yes.” “Lieutenant {{Anderson}} hasn’t arrived yet, but you can wait at his desk.”

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint ARRIVE AT POLICE STATION, with the template’s reception scenes (the two couples, the gate android, the receptionist). Narrated, no choice, no stat change. The wiki’s note that a surviving {{Todd}} can be filing a report at the station is not built: the template’s reception couple does not name him.

The Minister for Defense spoke of “intolerable provocation that cannot go unanswered”; the countries in the region have called for military forces to withdraw and for an international conference. Neither Moscow nor Washington has responded.

options.text: Research Lt. {{ANDERSON}} on the terminal.
options.fact: Research Lt. {{Anderson}}. “{{DETROIT}} POLICE DISMANTLE A NETWORK OF {{REDICE}} DEALERS”. February 3rd, 2028. More than 50 arrests throughout the country. {{Detroit}}’s finest has dealt a massive blow to the city’s growing {{RedIce}} epidemic, with a number of high-profile dealers and suppliers now behind bars and narcotics seized with a street value of $500,000. Detective {{Hank}} {{Anderson}}, a young but hugely talented Detective, is said to have been instrumental in the operation, which took months of planning. The DA described the work of Detective {{Anderson}} and his colleagues as “model investigative police work”. “DETECTIVE {{ANDERSON}} PROMOTED TO THE RANK OF LIEUTENANT”. August 22nd, 2029. Becoming the youngest lieutenant on the {{Detroit}} police force. Lieutenant {{Hank}} {{Anderson}} was among the most decorated Detectives in the police department’s recent history, securing a number of high-profile arrests and serving as an integral member of the force. Captain {{Fowler}} said the promotion was “long over-due”, describing {{Anderson}} as “among the most talented police I’ve ever worked with”. The new Lieutenant is expected to rise quickly through the ranks of the department and is already being tipped as a future Commissioner. “NEW RECORD SEIZURE OF {{REDICE}} IN {{DETROIT}}!” November 23rd, 2031. Nearly a ton of {{RedIce}} discovered in the hold of a boat after a long investigation conducted by Lieutenant {{Anderson}} of the {{Detroit}} police force.

adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND LT. ANDERSON, then the [ WAIT FOR HANK ] block before he arrives, as one repeatable scene: EXPLORE THE STATION (PowerPyx: “At Hank’s desk, sit in the chair in front of it briefly, then get up again”), EXAMINE HANK’S DESK and LEARN ABOUT HANK. The template’s clues, each its own option with the game’s scan title and sublines as the fact: KNIGHTS OF THE BLACK DEATH (“Listen to music”), the eight “Look at the desk” items (COFFEE CUP, JAPANESE MAPLE, DONUTS, DETROIT BASKETBALL CAP, ANTI-ANDROID SLOGANS, MATCHES, HAIRS, RED ICE TASK FORCE 2027; PowerPyx: “Scan the desk to find 8 clues”) and “Research LT. Anderson” (the three articles, offered once a desk item has been scanned, since LEARN ABOUT HANK follows EXAMINE HANK’S DESK on the chart). The nameplate, tissue and police-cases strings in the string table are not placed by the template and are not built. The headset, cap, stickers and hairs unlock {{Connor}}’s MUSIC, BASKETBALL, ANTI-ANDROIDS and DOG topics later. Also here, with no stat change: Officer {{Wilson}} (“Finding Hank’s desk”), Officer {{Chris}} (the template’s three variants), the call to {{Hank}} with the game’s LEAVE A MESSAGE / HANG UP buttons (calling at all is optional, as in the game), the man in the holding cell, and, only if the android was sent back to his cell in The Interrogation, TALK WITH CARLOS’ ANDROID, which plays the two cell scenes that follow. The scene ends either by going to the break room (TALK WITH GAVIN and the break-room TV) or by sitting down to wait; either way {{Hank}} arrives next. These two exits are listed first, as in the other repeatable scenes of this chapter the main line comes first. Simplifications: in the game the station can be explored in any order and also while {{Hank}} is in {{Fowler}}’s office; here the cell, the desk and the call come before {{Hank}} arrives, and the break room is the last stop before he does. The background chatter is quoted once; {{Wilson}}’s private phone call is not built; the magazines are a media scene after this one.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: {{Ivanoff}} Says “Niet”!
facts: {{Detroit}} Today, “{{Ivanoff}} Says ‘Niet’!”: after President {{Warren}} demanded that “all Russian troops withdraw from the arctic immediately”, the Russian president called her comments “megaphone diplomacy” and said “US sabre-rattling is the number one threat to stability in the region.” The Kremlin set out Russia’s claim to the territory in a detailed statement, and he would “remind President {{Warren}}” that “the United States is subject to UN conventions, like everybody else.” The conflict shows no signs of abating. On the cover: {{CyberLife}} is the world’s first trillion-dollar company; the global population has reached 10 billion.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Famous Painter Dies
facts: {{Detroit}} Today, “Famous {{Detroit}} Painter Dies”: the death of the artist {{Carl}} {{Manfred}} is confirmed; the coroner described a “fatal cardiac event” induced by a stressful domestic situation, and his son {{Leo}} has asked the media to respect the family’s privacy. {{Carl}} rose to fame in the 2020s as a figurehead of neo-symbolism, went through a dark period marked by alcohol and drugs, and had returned to work in recent months. The Governor called him “one of {{Detroit}}’s brightest lights”; his estate will auction a collection of his paintings. On the cover: the UN warns of World War Three; President {{Warren}} is at 33% approval.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: The Three Laws of Robotic Parenting
facts: {{Detroit}} Today, “The Three Laws of Robotic Parenting”: {{CyberLife}}’s child androids, once doubted, are now among its bestsellers: “Customizable, removable LED, no hunger, no expensive childcare... no smelly diapers!” With unemployment at 37.3%, $7,500 for a child that skips the teenage years and college looks like a wise investment against $350,000 over 17 years. A sociologist warns that these androids are leading fewer parents to have children when birthrates are already far too low (“the baby doom”); {{CyberLife}}’s director of humanization calls this “the usual resistance to new ideas” and the androids “a triumph of humanization design”. On the cover: the UN warns of World War Three; President {{Warren}} is at 33% approval.

media.title: the break-room news
facts: The break-room news: several sources report that {{CyberLife}} has provided the {{Detroit}} police with a prototype detective android. Police assistant androids have existed for several years, but this would be the first case of an android authorized to play an active role in criminal investigations; no one at {{CyberLife}} was available to comment.

Then the next report: the first book written by an artificial intelligence, “Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?”, has shot to the top of the bestseller list, and critics are unanimous in their praise. Designed by {{CyberLife}}, the AI known as VOLTAIRE analyzed human centers of interest on social networks for several months before its algorithms generated the plot; according to several specialists, most books written in the coming years will be the work of artificial intelligence.

media.title: the break-room news
facts: The break-room news: the police found the body of thirty-year-old {{CarlosOrtiz}} in his home last night, after calls from concerned neighbors. Known to the police as a petty criminal, he is reported to have suffered from a psychiatric condition and rarely left his apartment; he is thought to have died several weeks ago. The police appear to be treating the death as a homicide. His android is also reported missing.

Then the next report: the first book written by an artificial intelligence, “Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?”, has shot to the top of the bestseller list, and critics are unanimous in their praise. Designed by {{CyberLife}}, the AI known as VOLTAIRE analyzed human centers of interest on social networks for several months before its algorithms generated the plot; according to several specialists, most books written in the coming years will be the work of artificial intelligence.
